A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VUD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic uncertainty-decomposition experiments, bandit simulations, QA OOD detection, and MMLU abstention results in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and reports expanded QA abstention results in Table 2 and Figures 10, 66, and 67.

M1.justification: The variational estimators, auxiliary-query search, permutation ensembling, KL filtering, and classification/regression algorithms are retained. The new profiling and baseline-fitting explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Abstention evaluation expands from MMLU computer-science and moral questions to include BoolQA, HotpotQA, and PubMedQA, previously used for OOD detection. This extends an existing task to additional QA settings; the other dataset and task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The bandit comparators, four Martingale proxy likelihoods, and Deep Ensembles OOD comparator are retained. Abstention continues comparing aleatoric filtering, total-uncertainty filtering, and unfiltered predictions. Moving OOD results to Appendix G.5 does not remove its comparators.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix G.5 specifies 60 questions per MMLU abstention group; v3 Section 5.2 specifies 100 questions per evaluated QA group. V3 also evaluates multiple rejection thresholds beyond the retained 10% setting. Existing synthetic, bandit, and OOD protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures 10, 66, and 67 examine how AU-versus-TU filtering accuracy varies with the abstention threshold across five QA groups. V1 reports only the fixed-threshold abstention comparison. Existing sampling, permutation, dataset-size analyses, and the moral-question case study are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Table 10 reports abstention point estimates without uncertainty terms; v3 Table 2 adds ± quantities. Their statistical meaning and the abstention run count are not specified, so additional runs cannot be inferred. Existing OOD and bandit seed reporting is retained.

E6.justification: The abstention results are expanded and replaced under changed sample sizes. For example, MMLU-CS unfiltered/TU-filtered/AU-filtered accuracy changes from 76.67/83.33/85.19% in v1 Table 10 to 81.01/85.56/86.67% in v3 Table 2; this is not a same-setting performance gain. New binary-QA rows and threshold curves are added, including a BoolQA TU/AU tie at 85.56%. Existing bandit and OOD values are retained.

T1.justification: The variational-bound theorems, mathematical arguments, theoretical examples, and exchangeability assumptions in Appendices A, B, and D are retained. Appendix A.1 corrects the Va/Ua labels to Ve/Ue in an existing data-processing inequality without changing its proof argument.

C1.justification: The core claims about variational uncertainty bounds, approximate exchangeability, and desirable uncertainty behavior remain unchanged. Abstention replaces OOD detection as the highlighted downstream application in the introduction, but both applications and their benefit claims already appeared in v1.

C2.justification: V3 expands the bandit explanation: declining epistemic variance lets posterior mean reward dominate the exploration bonus, whereas total variance need not vanish. Appendix F also explains abstention through risk and coverage. The Bayesian-approximation limitations and interpretation of ambiguous moral questions are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix E.3 and Tables 5–6 document LLM calls per algorithm component. Appendix G.2 explicitly describes maximum-likelihood fitting of Martingale proxy parameters. Hardware, code access, and prompts remain unchanged, while v1's exact MMLU subset identifiers are omitted.

R1.justification: V3 adds eight references concerning hallucination, abstention, and deferral, including Feng et al., Gui et al., Kalai et al., and Kirichenko et al. A new Appendix F paragraph connects the application to selective classification; the central positioning against Bayesian and Martingale approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main QA discussion is rewritten around abstention, with the OOD discussion moved to Appendix G.5. V3 adds a profiling subsection and abstention-related discussion, relocates declarations to Appendix I, and updates the conference header. Most prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds three abstention figures and two profiling tables, expands and restructures the abstention table, and relocates the OOD table. Figure 2 is redrawn with the same dependency structure, and some existing plot panels are rearranged. The existing experimental graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: V1's small, single-threshold abstention demonstration becomes a broader evaluation with threshold-sensitivity evidence, while v3's computational accounting and baseline-fitting description improve transparency. These are useful but limited gains. The new abstention ± quantities remain unexplained, and the new curves misleadingly label retained fractions as fractions dropped. The core method and most supporting evidence are unchanged.
